name: isp_path_congestion
title: Congestion past the router
description: The local network stays clean; latency appears beyond the second hop. This is the case a single-layer tool always gets wrong.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 83 ms to send their first byte, about 65 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

evidence.label: name resolution phase of the synthetic request

card.title: Congestion past your router
card.summary: Your own network looks fine: your router answers in 4 ms. Past it, the path out is adding about 48 ms. That points to your internet connection or your provider rather than anything in your home.
remediation: Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.
If this keeps happening, export a diagnostic bundle and send it to your internet provider.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

evidence.label: RTT to the final responsive hop

card.title: Name lookups are slow
card.summary: Looking up addresses is taking 76 ms, well above normal for this network. DNS is the internet's phone book: when it is slow, pages feel slow to start even once they load fine.
remediation: Flush the DNS cache on this device.
Try a different DNS resolver in your network settings.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

evidence.label: median resolution time over the probe set
